cases.candidate_question: Can a constant divergence c replace the constant scalar curl hypothesis when computing counterclockwise circulation as c times area?
cases.mathematical_reason: No. The field (P,Q)=(-y,x) has divergence zero but scalar curl ∂xQ−∂yP=2. On every positive rectangle its counterclockwise circulation is twice the area, not zero. Green circulation uses scalar curl and its orientation, whereas Gauss outward flux uses divergence.
